column2: Ecosystems degrade with population, cities, industry, the conversion of forests into cropland, war and drought. Environmental laws and development help preserve them.

0–100 from the biome's base (rainforest 78, taiga 82, desert 62…): population per km² (up to −30), GDP per km² (up to −14), farmed land (up to −10), large river +3, development (−4 to +6), occupation −12 or war −4, and drought up to −10.
Every place receives water from rain and from the rivers that flow down from other areas. With more people and the same water, there is less per person.

0–100, with 1,700 m³ per person per year = 50 (each time the water per person is multiplied by 10, +56). In the province, 40% is its own water and 60% the country's. Dams and networks (development) add to it, and drought (up to −12) and population growth subtract. A drought also lowers the health of Public services.
A country can feed itself by producing or by buying abroad. Depending on imports is risky when grain prices rise or export bans appear.

0–100: self-sufficiency (produces what it eats = 60, double = 95), ability to import according to its wealth, world grain price against its trend, drought and war. If it imports food and grain prices rise, the health of Basic consumption and happiness drop.
Every biome has its plants and animals. When nature degrades — cities, crops, industry, war, drought or dams — the most sensitive species are the first to disappear.

Each species has a threshold: the biome's base health minus 10 (very sensitive), 20 (sensitive) or 32 (resilient). If the province's ecosystem falls below its threshold it becomes “At risk”; 12 points lower, “Endangered”. The cause is whatever subtracts the most from the ecosystem among its threats. They don't change the economy.
Countries with little water or little land produce it: they desalinate seawater (Israel, Saudi Arabia), irrigate (India, Egypt), grow in greenhouses (the Netherlands) or store water in dams.

Desalination plant (coast): +35 m³ per person per year per level, up to 3. Irrigation: +12% arable land and 10–20% bigger harvests per level, uses 4% of the water, up to 2. Greenhouses: food for 3% more of the population per level, even in drought, up to 3. Dam (river or hills): +8% water and drought takes half of it, +4% land; ecosystem health drops by 6. Cost: the province's GDP × 0.6–2% (more at each level). AI governments build them when their water or food is low.
Factories, mines and wells leave waste in the air, water and soil; treatment plants clean the wastewater before returning it to the rivers.

Your factories, mines, wells, construction firms, workshops and transport companies, the industrial companies on the stock exchange (headquartered in one of the 3 most populated provinces of their country) and the extraction from deposits subtract ecosystem health according to their size compared with the province's GDP (cap of 8 per source and 14 in total). Each level of treatment plant offsets half.
Many countries protect forests and watersheds with national parks and reforestation; Costa Rica nearly doubled its forest cover since the 1980s and lives off ecotourism.

Reforestation: +3 ecosystem and +1.5% water per level (up to 2; 24 months). Protected area: +5 ecosystem and +2% water (1; 12 months; government only). Treatment plant: offsets half of the pollution per level (up to 2; 18 months). They have upkeep every year (province GDP × 0.03–0.05% per level, between 6 and 10% of what the work cost); if it isn't paid, they are suspended that year. The tourism of your hotels, bars and jewelers rises or falls by up to 15% with the province's nature. The “Water technology” breakthrough makes all projects 20% cheaper.

Every province has its own nature: a biome, water, land to farm, and good and bad years.
  • 🌿 Card: tap a province and open the 🌿 Nature tab: its biome, ecosystem health, fresh water, food security (with what raises and lowers them), crops and resources, and the country summary.
  • 🏛️ Country → 🌿 Nature: water per person, food self-sufficiency, scarcity of each resource (oil, metals, grains…), provinces in drought and those with the least water.
  • 🌵 Droughts: each year some provinces have a drought: their harvests and GDP drop (almost all of it recovers the next year), as do their happiness and the health of Basic consumption and Public services.
  • ⚖️ Scarcity: if your country imports food or energy, it suffers when grain or oil prices rise; if it exports them, it gains.
  • 🗺️ Map: the 🌿 mode paints ecosystem health across the whole world.
  • 🦋 Flora and fauna: on each province's card you see its plants and animals; if the ecosystem degrades, you'll see which are at risk and why.
  • 🏗️ Projects: desalination plants, irrigation, greenhouses and dams raise a province's water and food. They take 12 to 36 months. If you govern, the treasury pays; if not, you can invest and they pay you back every year.
  • 🗺️ Rivers: in the map's 🌿 mode the main rivers show in blue.
  • 🌳 Conservation: reforest, declare protected areas or build treatment plants from each province's 🌿 tab. They raise ecosystem health and the water a little, attract tourism and cost upkeep every year.
  • 🏭 Pollution: your factories, mines and wells, the industrial companies on the stock exchange and the deposits subtract ecosystem health in their province according to their size.
  • 🌵 Drought and your farms: in a drought year your farms harvest less (up to 45%) and your ranches produce less (up to 25%).
  • 🔬 Water technology: with civil technology 3 your country gets it on its own; if you govern you can fund it sooner. It makes projects 20% cheaper.
